newsitem.title: USA: Xplor sets acquistions for stock.
newsitem.headline: Xplor sets acquistions for stock.

text.p: Xplor Corp said Monday it has agreed to two acquisitions for stock that will leave present holders with about 20 percent of the shares outstanding.

Xplor said it agreed to acquire substantially all of Venus Exploration Inc in exchange for 5,626,473 Xplor shares and a group of producing oil and gas properties from Lomak Petroleum Inc for 2,037,171 shares.
Xplor said it will also issue warrants to acquire 272,353 additional shares of its common stock to both Venus and Lomak.

Upon completion of the transactions, the company said, the stockholders of Venus, a private exploration and production company based in San Antonio, Texas, will own 58 percent of Xplor, and Lomak will own 22 percent.
Upon closing, Xplor said, its estimated proved oil and natural gas reserves will increase to about 12.0 billion cubic feet equivalent from 2.7 billion cubic feet at year end 1996.
Additionally, pro forma at March 31, 1997, the company will have over $2.5 million in cash, net of long-term debt, and a significant inventory of development and exploratory projects.

Upon completion of the transactions, Eugene L. Ames will assume the offices of chairman and chief executive officer of Xplor. Ames is currently chairman and chief executive of Venus. John Y. Ames, president of Venus, will be Xplor's President, and James E. Gayle, currently Xplor's chief executive, will become executive vice president.
Completion of the transactions, anticipated to occur before the end of the month, is subject to several closing conditions as well as approval by the stockholders of Venus. ((-- New
